question: Will no qualifying diplomatic US-Iran meeting occur by September 30, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
On June 22, the first round of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks in Switzerland concluded, with mediators reporting progress toward a roadmap for a final deal and follow-on technical talks expected to continue (see: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/22/us-iran-agree-on-roadmap-towards-final-deal-in-switzerland-talks).

This market will resolve according to the country in which the next formal senior-level round of peace talks between representatives of the United States and Iran begins by September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

A qualifying round must be a deliberate in-person diplomatic meeting or negotiating round concerning US-Iran relations, involving senior representatives of both the United States and Iran who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to conduct or materially direct diplomacy on behalf of their governments.

Indirect in-person diplomacy through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors will qualify, provided senior representatives of both the United States and Iran are participating in the same formal diplomatic process with the knowledge and authorization of their respective governments. The representatives need not be in the same room at the same time.

Follow-on technical talks from the June 22 Switzerland round will not qualify by themselves. Technical, staff-level, working-group, implementation, monitoring, preparatory, or deconfliction meetings will not qualify unless they occur as part of a new formally convened senior-level U.S.-Iran peace-talks round.

Brief greetings, chance encounters, photo opportunities, ceremonial appearances, or talks not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count.

The meeting must be in-person (including indirect in-person meetings) and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

If a qualifying round occurs in more than one country, resolution will be based on the country where the first qualifying senior-level diplomatic session begins.

If the next qualifying round begins in any country in the Middle East or North Africa other than the listed options, this market will resolve to “Other - Middle East/North Africa.”

If the next qualifying round begins in any country in Europe other than the listed options, this market will resolve to “Other - Europe.”

For purposes of this market, countries’ regions will be determined based on the U.S. State Department’s regional classifications in the “Countries and Areas List” (https://www.state.gov/countries-and-areas-list). Any country classified as part of “Europe and Eurasia” will be considered to be in Europe. Any country classified as part of “Near East (Middle East and North Africa)” will be considered to be in the Middle East/North Africa.

research:
I couldn't confirm any qualifying senior-level US-Iran round between June 22 and September 18, 2026. As of mid-September both sides were publicly saying no talks were scheduled. Fetching full pages failed through the proxy every time, so everything below comes from search-result summaries. Anything dated after 2026-09-18 is left out.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-06-21/22: Mediators Qatar and Pakistan said the US and Iran agreed a 60-day roadmap toward a final deal. The first senior round was held in Switzerland (reportedly at Bürgenstock, not Geneva). Technical talks were to start immediately, with working groups on nuclear issues, sanctions and monitoring. [Alaska Public/NPR](https://alaskapublic.org/news/national/2026-06-22/the-u-s-and-iran-agree-to-a-road-map-for-a-final-deal-mediators-say); [Nukta](https://nukta.com/us-iran-roadmap-final-deal-switzerland)
- The Al Jazeera page named in the criteria could not be fetched. Resolution depends on government statements or consensus media reports, and there is no single data series. The Polymarket market page ([link](https://polymarket.com/event/next-round-of-us-iran-peace-talks-byptptpt-20260623022722982)) also could not be fetched.

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-09-18)
- I found no publicly acknowledged senior-level round after June 22.
- 2026-09-15: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said there would be no talks with the US until Iran's conditions are met. He told people not to be "distracted" by Trump's mixed signals. The day before, Trump had said Tehran wanted a deal and talks could resume. [GlobalSecurity/IRNA](https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/library/news/iran/2026/09/iran-260915-irna01.htm); [The National](https://thenationalnews.com/news/gulf/2026/09/15/iran-dismisses-us-talks-as-hormuz-crisis-deepens)
- Mid-September: Rezaei's stated conditions were an end to the war and the naval blockade, release of frozen assets, and a region-wide ceasefire including Lebanon and Gaza. Reports also cite about $300B in compensation. [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/irans-rezaei-sets-sweeping-conditions-for-hormuz-reopening-as-us-talks-hit-new-impasse-1.500637980)
- So nothing settles the question yet. The status quo as of September 18 is no meeting.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-15: Iran rejected talks and tied reopening the Strait of Hormuz to US concessions (sources above).
- 2026-09-06/07: Araghchi spoke by phone with Turkey's FM Fidan and with Oman's FM about "developments in US-Iran talks." No venue or date was given. [Report.az](https://report.az/en/region/fidan-araghchi-discuss-latest-developments-in-us-iran-talks); [Gazette](https://gazettengr.com/?p=449330)
- About 2026-08-28: Trump said "I have no time schedule... I'm not in a hurry." A US administration source said the blockade would stay and no talks were scheduled. Qatari and Pakistani delegations were shuttling between capitals. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/28/iran-says-it-will-name-its-terms-for-reopening-strait-of-hormuz)
- 2026-08-17: The June MoU/roadmap period expired, although both sides had reportedly abandoned it weeks earlier. Spokesman Baghaei said the mediators are Pakistan and Qatar. [CGTN](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-08-17/news-1PGluxGqiVW/p.html)
- 2026-08-05: Axios reported a Strait of Hormuz deal was close, after calls between Witkoff, Araghchi and Oman's FM. I found no confirmation that it was carried out. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/05/us-iran-strait-of-hormuz-deal-nears)
- July 2026: US strikes and a naval blockade led Iran to halt negotiations and close Hormuz. Iran said the US had violated the MoU. Baghaei said there were "no negotiations," only messages passed through mediators. [ABC7](https://abc7ny.com/post/iran-war-update-mediators-see-progress-diplomatic-efforts-officials-say-no-negotiations-ongoing-us-baghaei-says/19584507/); [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/21/can-mediators-broker-a-truce-between-the-us-and-iran)

## 4. Base rates
- In 2026, senior rounds have been held in Muscat and Geneva (February), Islamabad (April, led by Vance, followed by a planned Witkoff/Kushner round) and Switzerland (June 22). That works out to roughly one senior round every 1 to 2 months while diplomacy was active. [Yeni Safak](https://en.yenisafak.com/world/irans-araghchi-talks-with-us-ongoing-no-conclusions-yet-3718889); [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/embed/2888752)
- Gaps have run longer after breakdowns. After the April Islamabad round, Iran refused to set a date until a framework was agreed. [Al-Monitor](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/04/iran-says-no-date-set-next-round-negotiations-us)
- The gap since June 22 is now about 88 days with no new round, the longest gap of 2026 that I found.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Early August 2026: Proactive Investors reported a Polymarket contract for a round starting by September 30 at about 71%. [Proactive](https://www.proactiveinvestors.co.uk/companies/news/1096429/traders-doubt-trump-s-monday-deadline-for-fresh-iran-talks-1096429.html)
- Undated (probably August to September): a timeline reported the "September 30" contract fell to 9% after Iran's Foreign Ministry denied talks were happening. [OSINT613](https://www.osint613.com/post/polymarket-odds-us-iran-meeting-rise-19489)
- July to August location-market snapshots: Pakistan was the favorite, Switzerland around 10%, Oman 7%, Qatar 5%, Egypt 1%, Turkey 1%, Iran 0%. These are stale. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/politics/next-iran-us-meeting-location-polymarket-odds-analysis); [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/will-the-next-diplomatic-us-iran-meeting-be-in-oman-by-september-30-2026-20260622185050764)
- A Manifold mirror exists. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Mana/next-round-of-usiran-peace-talks-by)
- I could not find a reliable price for the "no meeting" outcome as of September 18.

## 6. Upcoming events before September 30
- The UN General Assembly high-level week in New York (late September) is the most plausible setting for mediated contact, for example through Qatar. Whether any contact there counts depends on the criteria: it needs senior officials from both sides in a deliberately convened round, and indirect talks only qualify if senior representatives of both governments are taking part in the same formal process.
- Mediation by Qatar, Pakistan and Oman is ongoing. The Oman-Iran Hormuz corridor arrangement depends on the US accepting Iran's demands.
- Possible military escalation or blockade incidents in the Gulf, either of which could derail or speed up talks.
- The US midterms in early November; an Iranian official said Tehran may stall until after them. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/iran-stalling-on-deal-with-us-to-hurt-trump-politically-ahead-of-midterms-iranian-officials-say/)
